SMTO-PSM-0009 — The saved parameters in your request are too long

GUID: 05ea176c-5cd9-4991-83b1-81104f53987b
Slug: parameter-oversized
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • The saved parameters you mentioned with @ add up to more text than SMTO allows in one request. SMTO paused the task before starting it, and nothing was cut off or sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the message under your request. It shows how far over the limit you are and lists the largest parameters. Knowing which parameters are biggest tells you where trimming helps most.
  2. Select Edit request, remove the @ names you don't really need for this task, then select Apply correction. Each @ parameter adds all of its saved details to your request, so fewer parameters means less text.
  3. If you need them all, select Open Parameter Store, open the largest parameter, shorten its Context or Description text, select Save, then select Check again. Context, Description, Aliases and Tags all count toward the limit, not just the value.
  4. If you can't make them smaller, ask the person who manages SMTO to raise the parameter size limit. The limit is a server setting that only they can change.

What success looks like

  • The message under your request says the references were resolved, and the task starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete parameters just to make this task fit; other tasks may use them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The combined @ parameter block (header plus each entry's value, context, description, aliases and tags) exceeds agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars, so the task is held before inference.

What this means

  • The serialized reference block, including its header and all selected value/context/metadata projections, exceeds max_chars. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • The serialized reference block, including its header and all selected value/context/metadata projections, exceeds max_chars.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the total serialized reference allowance and which entries dominate it, including their descriptions and tags.

How to fix it

  • The Runtime message lists the total size, the limit and the five largest entries. Reference fewer entries, or shrink the largest entries' value, context, description, aliases or tags in Parameter Store, then choose Check again. To raise the limit, set AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_PROMPT_MAX_CHARS (agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars, default 4000) and restart the Server.
  • Reference fewer entries or reduce their stored context and value size before starting a new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete deliberately selected context fits the prompt-reference allowance without silent truncation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
